chapterTitle: FBISE Full-Book Annual Exam Simulator I (Comprehensive All Units 10–18)
subject: biology-10

questions.question: In woody tree stems, gaseous exchange between internal living tissues and the atmosphere takes place through: (FBISE Annual 2024)
questions.explanation: Lenticels are porous aerating tissue openings in the corky periderm of woody stems that allow gas diffusion.

questions.question: The funnel-shaped upper dilated end of the ureter inside the kidney that collects formed urine is the:
questions.explanation: Urine produced by nephrons drains through calyces into the renal pelvis, which funnels it down the ureter.

questions.question: The three protective connective tissue membranes covering the human brain and spinal cord are the: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: The brain and spinal cord are enclosed by the meninges: dura mater, arachnoid mater, and pia mater.

questions.question: The longest and strongest bone in the human skeleton is the:
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest, heaviest, and strongest weight-bearing bone in the human skeleton.

questions.question: In flowering plants, double fertilization results in the formation of a diploid zygote and a:
questions.explanation: The fusion of the second sperm nucleus with two polar nuclei produces a triploid (3n) primary endosperm nucleus.

questions.question: A cross between two individuals heterozygous for two traits (RrYy x RrYy) produces an F2 phenotypic ratio of: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: Mendels dihybrid cross demonstrates independent assortment, generating a characteristic 9:3:3:1 phenotypic distribution.

questions.question: Which of the following ecological pyramids is ALWAYS upright and can never be inverted under natural laws? (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Because energy is dissipated at every metabolic transfer step, an energy pyramid is always upright.

questions.question: The biological process in which soil nitrates are reduced back into gaseous molecular nitrogen (N2) is termed:
questions.explanation: Denitrification by anaerobic bacteria (e.g., Pseudomonas) returns fixed nitrogen back to the atmospheric reservoir.

questions.question: In genetic engineering, the small circular self-replicating extrachromosomal DNA used as a cloning vector is a:
questions.explanation: Plasmids are bacterial DNA rings engineered with restriction sites and antibiotic markers for foreign gene insertion.

questions.question: Which antimalarial drug was historically derived from the bark of the Cinchona tree? (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Quinine is an alkaloid isolated from Cinchona bark that was historically the premier clinical treatment for malaria.

questions.question: The physiological condition in which an individual exhibits severe physical or psychological distress when a drug is stopped is:
questions.explanation: Withdrawal syndrome manifests when dependent body systems experience sudden deprivation of an addictive substance.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the sparger in an industrial fermenter?

options.A: To circulate coolant water around the vessel
options.B: To bubble sterile air or oxygen through the liquid culture medium

questions.explanation: The sparger introduces pressurized sterile oxygen in microbubbles, ensuring adequate aeration for aerobic microbial growth.
